environment.cpu: Intel Core i9-13900HX; serial timing pinned to logical CPU 2 (performance core)
environment.configuration: 2D Release, C++23, -O2 (after global -O3), PCH ON, LTO OFF, compiler cache OFF, mold linker
environment.includes_filesystem: Kin worktree and dependency source on Linux partition; generated includes and build outputs on NTFS/FUSE
environment.timed_source_filesystem: Before/after translation-unit copies on the same NTFS/FUSE volume, with an identical explicit include path to the original private scripting headers
environment.host_activity: Other user jobs were running during parts of the session. All of our timed commands ran serially; no concurrent validation builds. Affinity does not remove thermal/frequency, memory, filesystem or other-process interference.

implementation.description: Represent only repeated captured callback signatures with std::function so sol2 can share invocation adapters. Unique signatures retain their lambdas. No public API or compiler flag changes.

main_clang_profile.note: Trace totals overlap and must not be summed. Profiling is separate from the uninstrumented paired measurements.

callback_compile_method: Three pairs per compiler, run 0/2 before then after and run 1 after then before. Compiler order Clang/GCC on even rounds, GCC/Clang on odd rounds. Same compiler commands and matching prebuilt -O2 target PCH; only source and output filenames differ. GNU time records wall/user/system/max RSS. No time trace, dependency/shader/PCH rebuild, archive or link in the timed commands.
optimization_method: Separate three-pair trial on the changed callbacks, alternating -O2/-O1 order as above. Both compilers use separately built matching -O1 PCHs; no invalid-PCH fallback. PCH setup is untimed. Only this translation unit is compared; all other target sources retain their existing settings.
runtime_method: Per compiler, link three probes against the existing engine libraries, inserting the measured workflow object before the scripting archive so the original workflow archive member is not selected. Baseline -O2, changed -O2 and changed -O1 objects use the same compiler. The -O1 variant changes this translation unit only. Probes run serially on CPU 2 in before/after/O1, reversed, then original order. Each process reports the upper median of 30 timed samples after three warmups. Reported summary is the median of three process results. Assertions stay enabled. Probe compilation/linking is outside runtime timing.

runtime_workloads.bind_50_vms_ms: Create 50 fresh Lua VMs, open base library, bind workflow API, and destroy them.
runtime_workloads.input_400000_calls_ms: 100000 iterations of held/pressed/released/axis on a declared inactive context. Check false action states, zero axis and returned iteration count. Three queries use changed adapters and axis is unchanged. Includes Lua loop/assert overhead.
runtime_workloads.tables_40000_calls_ms: 20000 iterations of controllers.devices and controllers.state(1), asserting empty device lists and disconnected player state. Devices uses a shared adapter; state remains unchanged. Includes table allocation, Lua loop/assert overhead.

rejected_or_unshipped_experiments.name: Wrap all 33 captured callbacks, including unique signatures
rejected_or_unshipped_experiments.status: Rejected after exploratory one-pair trial: little Clang gain and slower GCC; not part of the retained source or final summary.

rejected_or_unshipped_experiments.name: Initial shared-only trial
rejected_or_unshipped_experiments.status: Exploratory first pair; host load differed substantially. Replaced for summary purposes by the prescribed three-pair trial, retained here for transparency.

rejected_or_unshipped_experiments.name: -O1 workflow translation unit
rejected_or_unshipped_experiments.status: Measured but not shipped as a flag/preset. Faster single-file compilation, but slower sampled input queries. A whole-target development mode requires separate end-to-end and game runtime measurements.

limits: Only one translation unit is timed; these percentages are not whole-Kin or game build speedups.
Three pairs are local estimates on a busy hybrid-core laptop, not confidence intervals or a cross-platform guarantee. Absolute times differ across experiments.
Runtime probes exercise VM binding, inactive input queries and empty controller tables; they do not establish whole-game performance or cover every workflow operation.
O1 results cannot be extrapolated to the entire scripting target: other objects and Lua itself retain their normal optimization.
No Windows/MSVC, sanitizer or full 3D runtime validation in this round.

instructions: Use a separate worktree at base_commit and a separate persistent build per compiler. Configure with the environment flags above; build kin_lua, kin_lua_workflows2d_tests and the other listed validation targets first.
Before applying the callback diff, save the original source as before.cpp in a benchmark output directory, and capture kin_lua api --host for scene/entity/test/scenario into api-before/<host>.json.

Adjust paths in the embedded scripts to your worktree/build/output directories, and set an adequate TMPDIR. Apply the callback diff, then run workflow_measure.py 3, workflow_o1.py, workflow_runtime.py clang, workflow_runtime.py gcc and workflow_validate.py sequentially.

workflow_measure.py snapshots the changed source as after.cpp. The recorded formatted source differs only in whitespace/comments; the mechanical check verifies token equivalence and unmodified callback bodies/captures.

The workflow_runtime.py source shown is the final compiler-parametrized version; the initial Clang run used the same commands/workloads before parametrization. Runtime samples and commands are retained above.

import hashlib,json,os,pathlib,subprocess
base=pathlib.Path('/mnt/windows/Users/amedeo/Desktop/gamedev');out=base/'kin-workflow-build-bench';results=[]
pattern='^(kin-(scripting|entity-scripts|lua-script|lua-workflows2d|lua-runtime|lua-tooling|scene|scene-asset|scene-workflow2d)|hex-demo|shapes-demo)$'
targets=['kin_lua','kin_lua_script_tests','kin_scripting_tests','kin_entity_scripts_tests','kin_lua_workflows2d_tests','kin_lua_runtime_tests','kin_scene_tests','kin_scene_asset_tests','kin_scene_workflow2d_tests','hex_demo','shapes_demo']
for compiler in ['clang','gcc']:
 build=base/('kin-build-time-clang' if compiler=='clang' else 'kin-build-time-out');tmp=base/('kin-workflow-tests-'+compiler);tmp.mkdir(exist_ok=True);env={**os.environ,'TMPDIR':str(tmp),'SDL_VIDEODRIVER':'dummy','SDL_AUDIODRIVER':'dummy'}
 with (out/(compiler+'-validation-build.log')).open('w') as f:subprocess.run(['cmake','--build',str(build),'--parallel','4','--target',*targets],env=env,stdout=f,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,check=True)
 print('Built '+compiler,flush=True)
 with (out/(compiler+'-tests.log')).open('w') as f:subprocess.run(['ctest','--test-dir',str(build),'--output-on-failure','-j','2','-R',pattern],env=env,stdout=f,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,check=True)
 print('Passed 11 selected tests: '+compiler,flush=True)
 reports={};api=out/('api-after-'+compiler);api.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
 for host in ['scene','entity','test','scenario']:
  result=subprocess.run([str(build/'bin/kin_lua'),'api','--host',host],env=env,text=True,capture_output=True,check=True);(api/(host+'.json')).write_text(result.stdout);report=json.loads(result.stdout);assert report==json.loads((out/'api-before'/(host+'.json')).read_text()),(compiler,host)
  reports[host]=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(report,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest()
 results.append({'compiler':compiler,'selected_tests_passed':11,'test_regex':pattern,'api_matches_main':reports});(out/'validation-results.json').write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2)+'\n')
 print('All four API reports match main: '+compiler,flush=True)

def normalize(v):return re.sub(r'\s+','',re.sub(r'//[^\n]*','',v))
assert normalize(s)==normalize(final)
for _ in range(12):
 m=re.search(r'\w+\["[^"]+"\] = (std::function<[^\n]+>\{)\s*(?=\[)',s);assert m
 start,end=m.span(1);body=s.index('{',end);depth=0;state=None;j=body
 while j<len(s):
  c=s[j];n=s[j:j+2]
  if state in ['"',"'"]:
   if c=='\\':j+=2;continue
   if c==state:state=None
  elif state=='line':
   if c=='\n':state=None

   if n=='*/':state=None;j+=2;continue

  elif n=='/*':state='block';j+=2;continue
  elif c in ['"',"'"]:state=c
  elif c=='{':depth+=1
  elif c=='}':
   depth-=1
   if depth==0:break
  j+=1
 assert s[j+1:j+3]=='};'
 s=s[:start]+s[end:j+1]+s[j+2:]
s=s.replace('#include <functional>\n','')
